r.정치 구도: The president is directly elected but holds a largely ceremonial role, and the government is led by a prime minister chosen by the lower house. Several members are elected in each constituency, with voters ranking candidates in order of preference, so independents are numerous and coalition governments are the norm. The two long-dominant centrist parties trace their split to the civil war fought over the 1921 treaty with Britain, yet today they govern together in coalition. Sinn Féin, which campaigns for unity with Northern Ireland, won the most first-preference votes in the 2020 election and has grown into the main opposition. In the 2025 presidential election a left-wing independent backed by the opposition parties won by a landslide, and housing costs and rents are now the dominant issue.

t.why: A low-tax, English-speaking EU member, it hosts the European headquarters of US tech firms such as Apple, Google and Meta, as well as many drugmakers. That keeps it in the news over tax: in 2024 the EU Court of Justice ruled that tax breaks Ireland had given Apple were illegal state aid and ordered it to recover 13 billion euros. Since Britain left the EU, keeping the border with Northern Ireland open and protecting the 1998 Good Friday Agreement have been at the heart of its foreign policy. It is militarily neutral and not a member of NATO, and a bill to scrap the rule requiring UN approval for overseas troop deployments remains hotly contested. In 2024 it recognized Palestine as a state together with Spain and Norway, and in the second half of 2026 it holds the presidency of the Council of the EU.
t.rel: It shares an island with the UK and borders Northern Ireland. It keeps military neutrality and has not joined NATO, and within the EU it hosts many US companies' European headquarters.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in 1983. Korea opened an embassy in Dublin in 1987, and Ireland opened one in Seoul in 1989. Long before that, in 1933, Irish priests of the Missionary Society of St. Columban arrived and worked in South Jeolla Province and on Jeju. One of them founded St. Isidore Farm on Jeju in 1961 to help poor farmers stand on their own feet, and in 2018 he was made an honorary citizen of Korea. Since a working holiday agreement took effect in 2010, several hundred young Koreans a year have gone to Ireland to work and learn English.
t.know: The potato famine once sharply reduced its population, and a very large Irish diaspora lives abroad.
etext: Low corporate tax, the English language and access to the EU single market drew US tech, pharmaceutical and medical-device companies to set up European headquarters and plants. Because their profits are booked in Ireland, GDP looks much larger than living standards would suggest.
Plentiful grassland makes it easy to raise cattle outdoors, so it exports large amounts of dairy and beef. Food brands such as its butter and whiskey are well known abroad.

Corporate tax receipts depend on a handful of big US firms, so if they leave or the United States changes its tax and tariff policies, the public finances could take a heavy hit. A housing shortage keeps prices and rents very high, and roads and the power grid are struggling to keep up with a growing population.
